## Data used

* BCI Competition IV 2a, all 9 participants, both sessions, left-hand vs right-hand imagery only (classes 3 and 4 are excluded as outside the task and are counted, not hidden).
* **2346 trials** after rejection; class counts {'0': 1165, '1': 1181} (0 = left, 1 = right).
* Rejected left/right trials: **246** — reasons: {'expert artifact marker (1023)': 246}. Full list: `outputs/final_v1/rejected_trials.csv`.
* Epoch: 0.5–2.5 s after cue onset; band-pass [4.0, 40.0] Hz (CSP: [8.0, 30.0] Hz); features: log mean PSD in {'mu': [8.0, 12.0], 'beta_low': [13.0, 20.0], 'beta_high': [21.0, 30.0]}.
* Spatial grid 16×16, cubic interpolation, montage `colin27_1020`.

## Protocol A - same participant, unseen session (train T → test E)

Question answered: *can a model calibrated on one person's first session be used on the same person on another day?* Training uses only that participant's session T (the last run of T is the CNN's validation set; logistic-regression C is chosen by run-grouped 5-fold CV); the test set is that participant's session E. Each model therefore trains on roughly 110–140 trials (the CNN on about one run fewer, which is held out for validation).

Evaluated participants: **9**; training participants per fold: 1 (their own session T).

## Protocol B - unseen participant (leave-one-subject-out)

Question answered: *does a model transfer to a participant it has never seen?* For every held-out participant, all their trials (both sessions) are held out of training **and** model selection; the CNN is validated on two other whole participants (the next two IDs, a fixed rule); logistic-regression C is chosen by subject-grouped 5-fold CV inside the 8 training participants.

Evaluated participants: **9**; training participants per fold: 8.

## How to read these numbers

* Chance level for balanced accuracy is 0.5. With ~110–280 test trials per participant, an accuracy needs to be roughly 0.55–0.59 to be distinguishable from chance for *that participant* (last column above, one-sided binomial test, p<0.05, uncorrected).
* The two protocols are different questions. Protocol A numbers must not be presented as evidence of cross-participant generalisation, and vice versa.
* The spread between participants (std column; best vs worst participant) is as important as the mean.
* No comparison with published results is made: published BCI Competition IV 2a results mostly concern the 4-class problem with different splits and metrics (e.g. Cohen's kappa), so they are not comparable with the binary balanced-accuracy numbers above.
* The CNN did **not** outperform the classical baselines in this experiment. Possible reasons (hypotheses, not tested): few training trials per participant in protocol A, a coarse 16×16 grid for 22 electrodes, power features without phase/spatial-filter information, no hyper-parameter tuning for the CNN, strong between-participant differences in protocol B.

#### Paired participant-level comparisons on the primary results (n = 9; Holm-corrected within protocol)

| Protocol | Comparison | mean diff. BA | bootstrap 95 % CI | exact Wilcoxon p | Holm-adjusted p |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A (same participant, unseen session) | csp_lda − logreg | +0.137 | [+0.103, +0.180] | 0.004 | 0.012 |
| A (same participant, unseen session) | csp_lda − cnn | +0.176 | [+0.132, +0.221] | 0.004 | 0.012 |
| A (same participant, unseen session) | logreg − cnn | +0.039 | [+0.005, +0.072] | 0.129 | 0.129 |
| B (unseen participant, LOSO) | csp_lda − logreg | +0.057 | [-0.019, +0.137] | 0.359 | 0.387 |
| B (unseen participant, LOSO) | csp_lda − cnn | +0.087 | [+0.012, +0.182] | 0.164 | 0.387 |
| B (unseen participant, LOSO) | logreg − cnn | +0.030 | [-0.000, +0.065] | 0.129 | 0.387 |

Wilcoxon exact p-values with n = 9 cannot go below 0.0039; the bootstrap interval resamples participants (not trials) and is itself coarse at n = 9.


## Reproduce

```bash
python -m src.training.train evaluate --protocol cross_session loso --name final_v1 --status final
python scripts/make_experiment_report.py final_v1
```

Seeds: `evaluation.seed` = 42 (+ participant ID for the CNN). Exact numerical reproducibility of the CNN can depend on the PyTorch version, CPU and thread count; classical models are deterministic given the data.
